confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web searches of cost-of-living sites (Numbeo, CityCost and whereandwhen). These sites put a cappuccino at about $1.6–1.9, local draught beer at about $1.2–2.0 and an inexpensive meal at about $4–4.5. They put a mid-range meal for two at $25–40, so I chose a middle figure. The sources partly disagree, and CityCost says some of its data is AI-generated. My figures lean a little toward tourist-area prices because July is peak season. I did not search directly for cocktail and wine prices. I estimated them from the local price relationship to beer, plus the high cost of imported spirits and wine in Egypt's tourist venues, so they are less certain. Accommodation figures are my own estimates from general knowledge. I did not check any live booking sites or listings. Hurghada has few registered hostels, which makes the dorm and private-room figures the least certain. For FX, I used the RBA 4pm indicative rate for 18 November 2026, as reported in the search result for the RBA exchange rates page.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with other Egyptian Red Sea resorts such as Sharm El Sheikh and Marsa Alam, and with Egypt's countrywide price levels after the devaluation of the Egyptian pound.
